assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offers bargaining is a foundational result in non-cooperative game theory. It gives a tractable, unique subgame-perfect solution that links bargaining power to impatience. It also underpins the strategic foundations of Nash bargaining and decentralized market models, and it is used across labour, trade, industrial organisation, search and matching. The influence on later theory is broad and durable, and the work meets a high bar for originality and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the clear originator. The Rubinstein–Wolinsky (1985) bargaining-in-markets work extends the idea to decentralized trade and links bargaining to search. Binmore made important related contributions, including the Binmore–Rubinstein–Wolinsky synthesis, but a cap of three laureates and the clarity of the two core papers make Rubinstein and Wolinsky the most defensible pair.
assessment.maturity: More than four decades of confirmation, with textbook status and extensive application. There is no timing risk beyond the age of the contributors.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would also want to credit Binmore's contributions.
Whether the strong theory-and-foundations profile is weighed against applied or empirical impact in this cycle.
Rubinstein's later contributions to bounded rationality and economic theory could change how the prize citation is framed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, built from nominal rigidities, microfounded Phillips curves and interest-rate rules, is the dominant paradigm of modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice. It has changed how policy is designed and communicated. The importance of the field is very high.
assessment.attribution: Credit is diffuse. Calvo (time-dependent pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the Taylor rule), Woodford (the integrative microfounded synthesis), Gali (the empirical and theoretical NK monetary framework), Christiano–Eichenbaum–Evans (medium-scale DSGE estimation) and Smets–Wouters all matter. A three-person cap forces hard choices. I propose Woodford, Taylor and Gali as a defensible core, while recognizing that Calvo and Christiano–Eichenbaum are plausible alternatives.
assessment.maturity: Decades of validation in policy practice and academic work. The post-2021 inflation episode and the debates about HANK extensions and the limits of the framework add some uncertainty, though these probably refine rather than undermine the core contribution.
uncertainties: Attribution among at least six or seven strong claimants.
Whether the committee prefers a narrower citation, such as the pricing friction or the policy rule.
Gertler appears on this list but also in B003, so the lists overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and the amplification of shocks through credit are central to understanding business cycles and financial crises. Kiyotaki–Moore (1997) credit cycles and Bernanke–Gertler / Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist financial accelerator models shaped post-2008 macro-finance and policy thinking. The framework is widely used in macro modelling.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clearest originators of the collateral-driven credit-cycle mechanism. Gertler contributed to the financial accelerator and to later macro-finance models of intermediary frictions. Bernanke already shared the 2022 prize for banking and financial crises, so the accelerator side partly overlaps with an existing award, and Gilchrist's role is more empirical and secondary.
assessment.maturity: Established for about 30 years, with strong reinforcement from the 2007–09 crisis and the large subsequent literature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 award, which covered banks and financial crises and could make the committee cautious.
Whether Gertler or Gilchrist should be credited for the accelerator tradition versus Kiyotaki and Moore alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed international trade theory after the new trade theory. Melitz (2003) is among the most cited and influential trade papers, and it reshaped how gains from trade, productivity reallocation and welfare are analysed and measured. Helpman's work extended the framework to heterogeneous firms, offshoring and the labour-market effects of trade. This is substantial, original and broadly adopted.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the clear originator of the heterogeneous-firm trade model. Helpman has additional claims through his work on trade with firm heterogeneity and on firm-level trade patterns. Krugman won in 2008 for new trade theory, which would need to be distinguished. Redding is a major contributor to quantitative and spatial extensions but is arguably less of an originator.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of confirmation across theory, structural estimation and empirical work, with strong policy use in trade evaluation.
uncertainties: Possible empirical-credit claims by others, such as Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are not on the list.
Overlap with Krugman's 2008 prize.
Helpman also appears in B030, and the committee might group his work differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work on import competition from China, tasks and technology, and polarisation of labour demand is highly influential. It has shaped public debate and academic research on wage inequality, regional adjustment and political effects. The work combines credible empirical design with a clear conceptual framework (the task-based approach).
assessment.attribution: The China-shock evidence is mainly Autor–Dorn–Hanson. The task approach is also associated with Autor–Levy–Murnane, and with Acemoglu, who shared the 2024 prize for institutions, and Katz. Restricting the citation to Autor, Dorn and Hanson is cleaner for the trade-shock agenda but leaves out other major strands.
assessment.maturity: A research programme of about 15 years, with ongoing debate about long-run magnitudes and robustness. Substantial replication and extension, but still more contested than the older theory candidates.
uncertainties: Some findings have been questioned, for example on identification and persistence.
Overlap with the 2021 empirical-labour prize and the 2024 prize.
Whether the committee would rather credit the task framework than the trade shock.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The long-run top-income and wealth data series, built from tax records, changed the empirical basis of research and public debate on inequality. Offshore wealth estimates added a related agenda. The work has had very large academic, data-infrastructure and policy impact, and it created a research programme (the World Inequality Database).
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the principal originators of the top-income series, and Zucman of the offshore and wealth-distribution estimates. Atkinson, who is deceased, was a precursor. Credit for conceptual theory, such as r > g, is more contested than the data contributions.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of work. Measurement choices, especially for wealth and for post-tax income, remain debated, and the policy conclusions are more disputed than the data construction.
uncertainties: Methodological controversy over wealth-inequality estimates and some tax-data adjustments.
Whether the committee treats this as measurement or as theory and policy advocacy.
Saez also appears in B034, which could affect how his contributions are grouped.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Present bias (quasi-hyperbolic discounting), models of self-control and reference-dependent preferences extended behavioural economics from documented anomalies to formal, portable models. They have applications to savings, consumption, health and contract design. Thaler (2017) and Kahneman (2002) already represent behavioural work, but this strand is theoretical and distinct.
assessment.attribution: Laibson (1997) and Rabin, in work with O'Donoghue and with Koszegi, are central. Loewenstein is important on intertemporal choice and psychology, but his contribution is more psychological than formal. The choice among five names is difficult, and a three-person cap leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Two to three decades of influence. Field evidence is strong for present bias, and weaker or more mixed for some reference-dependence applications.
uncertainties: Overlap with existing behavioural awards and a possible reluctance to give a further behavioural prize.
Mixed field evidence for loss aversion and reference points.
Attribution among Laibson, Rabin, O'Donoghue, Koszegi and Loewenstein.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine learning methods for causal inference, including double/debiased ML, causal forests and heterogeneous treatment effects, extend credible empirical practice to high-dimensional settings. Their use is spreading rapidly in economics, policy evaluation and industry. The methodological contribution is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Chernozhukov and co-authors developed the double ML and high-dimensional inference framework. Athey and Wager developed causal forests and the related heterogeneous-effect methods, with Imbens as an important collaborator. Imbens shared the 2021 prize, which complicates the attribution. Wager is relatively junior. A pair of Athey and Chernozhukov covers the two main strands but is not obviously complete.
assessment.maturity: Ten years or more of influence, with fast adoption. Long-run durability compared with older methodological contributions is not yet established, so this candidate is probably less mature than most of the higher-ranked ones.
uncertainties: Timing, because the field is still evolving and may see consolidation.
Overlap with the 2021 causal-inference prize.
Athey also appears in B024, so her contributions are split across lists.
